DNS Spoofing, also known as DNS cache poisoning, involves adversaries manipulating DNS settings to redirect users from legitimate websites to malicious ones. This can be achieved by injecting false DNS responses into the cache of a DNS resolver, causing users to be directed to incorrect IP addresses when they attempt to access certain domains. The attack can lead to various malicious outcomes, such as preventing access to legitimate sites or facilitating the installation of malware on the user's device [Source 1]. 

Additionally, adversaries may exploit vulnerabilities in DNS protocols to gain unauthorized access or control over user credentials and other sensitive information [Source 2].
